quote: You just need to be on the title of the home and have a credit score of 670.
stewart_read: Rep merges the title qualifier and credit qualifier awkwardly into one run-on line, and the customer immediately disputes it without the rep clarifying or correcting.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be intentional simplification for speed, but the customer's direct pushback ('That's not right') shows it landed as inaccurate, not efficient.
coaching_implication: Slow down and state qualifiers as two distinct, clear asks so the customer isn't left correcting the rep.

stewart_read: Customer flags the qualifier statement as wrong and the rep never circles back to clarify what was actually inaccurate.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged it a minor point not worth re-litigating to keep momentum, but silence here leaves a credibility gap unresolved.
coaching_implication: Any direct factual pushback from a customer needs at least a one-line acknowledgment/correction before moving on.

stewart_read: A striking bill figure is given and the rep does not flip it, react to it, or use it as leverage anywhere in the rest of the call.
coaching_implication: This is the single biggest anchor miss on the call — the rep should have echoed the number back and tied it to the utility grievance the customer raises later at 03:58.

stewart_read: Customer volunteers escalating bill figures unprompted — a second, stronger anchor than the earlier $1,000 estimate — and the rep lets it pass without reflection.
coaching_implication: Rep should have caught this rising-cost detail and used it as the emotional hook: 'that's exactly the kind of increase solar protects you from.'

quote: You already you you shut green solar down our our throat. You're making us pay for wind turbines that we don't want.
stewart_read: Customer is venting frustration at the utility/green energy system in language that is a gift-wrapped setup for the bill-as-villain flip, and the rep only responds with 'Mhmm.'
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this a rant not worth engaging to avoid derailing further, but the passive response wastes a strong emotional opening.
coaching_implication: This is the ideal moment to pivot: 'That's exactly why customers switch — stop paying the utility for power you could generate yourself.'

quote: can I send it to you in a picture or a text from this number?
stewart_read: Customer offers to send the bill photo directly but the rep redirects to a separate 801 number and a future text exchange instead of capturing it live.
alternative_hypothesis: Landline constraint may be real (rep says 'this number... is a landline'), making the redirect a legitimate technical necessity rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: If landline is confirmed, rep should still lock a specific time to expect the text reply rather than leaving it fully open-ended.

quote: we can get the next phone call scheduled over text for you
stewart_read: Call ends with no day/time agreed and no 'is that fair?' handshake — the entire next step is deferred to an unscheduled future text.
coaching_implication: Rep should have proposed a concrete callback window even if the bill photo wasn't yet received.
